messages.subject: customNextItem and 'ordered' constraint (mirtCAT)
parts:
Dear All,

I was wondering how to properly combine a customNextItem function with the 'ordered' constraint in case of testlets.

Currently, I am working on a testlet-based shadow CAT, which works fine with the 'ordered' constraint and custom constraint function. However, when implementing a customNextItem function (to calculate a different selection criterion, in this case the mean information of the testlet), it seems that the customNextItem overrides the 'ordered' constraint, and only single items are selected. It does not work properly if I pass the design-object to the customNextItem function (via design_elemtents = TRUE).

Perhaps somebody has an idea?

Thanks in advance!

Best wishes
Chris

messages.subject: Re: customNextItem and 'ordered' constraint (mirtCAT)
parts: On Thu, Feb 6, 2020 at 5:08 PM Chris Koenig <koenig...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear All,

I was wondering how to properly combine a customNextItem function with the 'ordered' constraint in case of testlets.

Currently, I am working on a testlet-based shadow CAT, which works fine with the 'ordered' constraint and custom constraint function. However, when implementing a customNextItem function (to calculate a different selection criterion, in this case the mean information of the testlet), it seems that the customNextItem overrides the 'ordered' constraint, and only single items are selected. It does not work properly if I pass the design-object to the customNextItem function (via design_elemtents = TRUE).

Shadow CAT implementation in mirtCAT will entirely ignore the constraints such as 'ordered' and such, largely because their implementation is quite different for item selection (the non-shadowcat method uses ad-hoc selection methods to create such effects, while the latter obviously must select item in order to fulfill the complete show session). Within the custom customNextItem() function you'd likely have to evaluate the shadowCAT next item, and if the item falls within the testlet select the first item in the ordered testlet set. I imagine this will be a little clunky, though it may be possible to create a more elegant solution through modifying the supplied item parameters (it's not completely obvious how to do this, so I'll think a little more about a potential workaround). HTH.

Phil
